_comment: Known disagreements between the workbench's response checks and the official HL7 FHIR Validator (HL7ValidatorConformanceTest). At most 5 entries, each with one reason and one open issue; each item records the verdict pair it expects. An item that starts to agree fails the test until it is removed. Do not add an entry to make a new disagreement pass without a reason and an issue (README.md in this directory).

entries.reason: Deliberate leniency in fhir-crd-router's CoverageInformationValidator: the HL7 CRD reference implementation (which Fabrikam imitates) sends the pre-2.x 'identifier' sub-extension in place of coverage-assertion-id, and the router reports it as a WARNING. The validator reports a missing coverage-assertion-id slice and an undefined sub-extension (errors).

Deliberate strictness in fhir-crd-router: the coverage sub-extension is Reference(Coverage), and 'Patient/pat-synthetic-001' names a Patient. The validator does not check the type of an unresolved literal reference.

The validator judges cards with hl7.fhir.uv.tools.r4#1.1.2's CDSHooksResponse logical model, which is looser than CDS Hooks 2.0: cards is 0..* and indicator 0..1 where the spec says REQUIRED, and summary has no 140-character limit. An action's description is 0..1 (cds-resp-5 requires it only on suggestion actions, and the validator applies no action invariant to systemActions), and nothing requires resource for create or update, which the spec's Action table does. The workbench follows the spec text.

The validator applies FHIR JSON's rule that arrays are never empty to CDS Hooks JSON, so it rejects "systemActions": []. CDS Hooks 2.0 is plain JSON and does not forbid empty arrays (it requires "cards": [] when there are none).
